results.text: {"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes monthly invoice splitting by gut feel and names no key-to-owner map, no weekly coverage figure, and no reconciled or aged untagged remainder, so no walk or run artefact is supported."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a key-to-owner mapping (each API key maps to a named owning team) and a weekly coverage figure posted every Monday, which meets the walk artefact requirement, but it does not mention reconciling coverage to the invoice or owning and aging the untagged remainder, so the run requirement is not supported."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The statement describes a monthly reconciliation of coverage to the invoice at 97 percent, with the untagged remainder owned and aged (oldest item 11 days), which meets the run artefact requirements, and it does not cancel or contradict the walk artefacts (key-to-owner map and weekly coverage figure), which are implied by the run artefact under the rubric's inclusion rule."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement is a claim of best-in-class attribution and general awareness ('everyone knows'), with no described artefact such as a key-to-owner map, a weekly coverage figure, or a reconciliation to the invoice, so it does not meet the walk or run requirements."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a key-to-owner map and a weekly coverage figure of 90 percent, which meets the walk artefacts, but the reconciliation to the invoice is only a plan for next year, so the run artefact is not supported."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement claims 99 percent coverage but describes no key-to-owner map, no weekly coverage figure, and no invoice reconciliation; the shared bucket is a catch-all that lacks the owned, aged remainder the run level requires, so no walk or run artefact is described."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes reacting to provider dashboards after a surprising bill and names no gateway log with one record per call, so no walk or run artefact is described."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a gateway that writes one record per model call with model, tokens, owner and cost, which is the walk artefact, but it does not mention any monthly reconciliation of those records to the invoice, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The statement describes gateway records reconciled line by line to the invoice every month within a stated 0.5 percent tolerance, which meets the run artefact, and it implies the per-call gateway log of the walk artefact by referencing gateway records and their line-by-line reconciliation."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement claims 'full observability' with a 'modern tracing platform' but does not describe a gateway log with one record per call, nor any reconciliation of records to invoice lines, so it names no qualifying artefact and falls to crawl."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a gateway that records every call and its cost, which is the walk artefact (a gateway log with one record per call), but it does not describe reconciliation of those records to the invoice line by line within a stated tolerance, so the run requirement is not met; the finance team's trust is a claim rather than an artefact and does not raise the level."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement claims totals match the invoice monthly but describes no gateway log with one record per call (the walk artefact) and no line-by-line reconciliation within a stated tolerance (the run artefact), so it does not meet walk or run."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes cost per token and cost per call, which are unit-cost metrics rather than cost per outcome, and it names no signed artefact for any product, so neither the walk nor the run requirements are met."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes one artefact, a cost per resolved ticket for the support assistant, with 'resolved' defined and signed by its product owner, which meets the walk requirement, but it does not show cost per outcome for every material product with failures in the numerator, a distribution, or board-pack inclusion, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The statement describes an artefact covering all six material products with cost per outcome including retries and failures in the numerator, reported as median and 95th percentile (a distribution) and carried in the board pack, which satisfies every Run requirement, and it contains no clause cancelling the walk artefact."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement is a claim of strong margins using adjectives ('strong', 'healthy') without describing any cost-per-outcome artefact, owner-signed or otherwise, so it does not meet the walk requirement and certainly not run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes cost per outcome reported for three of six products with failures included, which meets the walk artefact (cost per outcome for one product), but it does not show the run requirements: coverage is only half of the material products, there is no described distribution, and the board summary is not shown to be the board pack containing per-product cost per outcome as a distribution, nor is there a statement extending run-level artefacts to the walk artefact."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes an average cost per successful task across products that excludes retried runs, which means failures are left out of the numerator and the figure is not a distribution, so it meets neither the walk artefact (a cost per outcome for one product signed by its owner) nor the run artefact requirements."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes a naive heuristic (last month's bill plus twenty percent) rather than a driver-based forecast, and it contains no backtest, error budget, variance split, or change register, so it does not meet the walk or run artefact requirements."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a driver-based model (calls, tokens per call, price, mix) with a six-month backtest and a reported median error, which meets the walk artefact, but it names no error budget, no variance split by driver, and no register of changes, so the run requirements are not met."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a driver forecast with an error budget, monthly variance split by driver, and a register of changes, but it never mentions a backtest, so the walk artefact (driver-based forecast with a backtest) is not confirmed and the run requirement cannot be met, leaving the highest supported level at walk only if the driver forecast itself is taken as the walk artefact, which it is not since the backtest is absent; therefore the statement supports only crawl."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement only claims use of 'advanced predictive analytics' without describing any artefact, such as a driver-based forecast, a backtest, an error budget, variance decomposition, or a change register, so it does not meet the walk or run requirements."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company describes an existing driver-based forecast with a backtest, which meets the walk artefact, while the register of changes is only planned for next quarter and so cannot count toward run, and no error budget or variance split by driver is described."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The company describes a driver-based forecast with monthly variance explanation, but explicitly states it has never backtested the forecast, so the Walk artefact (driver-based forecast with a backtest) is absent and the Run requirements cannot be met either."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes only spikes being noticed in a monthly review meeting, with no daily spend alerts (walk artefact) and no per-product rate alerts with owners, runbooks, history replay, or time-to-stop measurement (run artefact)."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company describes a daily spend alert that fires to a channel when spend exceeds 130 percent of the trailing average, which satisfies the walk artefact of daily spend alerts, but it does not mention per-product rates, owners, runbooks, historical replay, or time-to-stop measurement, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The statement describes rate alerts (call-rate and cost-per-session) per product, each with an owner and runbook, replayed on 90 days of history, and a measured 14-minute median time to stop, which together satisfy every run artefact requirement, and it does not cancel or contradict the implied walk artefact of daily spend alerts."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement is a general claim about being AI-powered and catching issues before they affect the bill, with no described artefact such as daily spend alerts, per-product rate alerts with owners and runbooks, or historical replay and time-to-stop measurement, so it does not reach the walk level."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The company describes per-product rate alerts with owners and runbooks, which satisfies the walk requirement of daily spend alerts (rate alerts are at least that), but it explicitly states the alerts have never been replayed on history, so the run requirement (replayed on history with time-to-stop measured) is not met and the walk artefact cannot be inferred to carry the run level."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes daily alerts firing on spend, which satisfies the walk artefact, but it does not describe per-product rate alerts with owners and runbooks, nor any historical replay, so the run requirements are not met."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes a quarterly-updated spreadsheet budget, which is not a per-team budget with an alert at a threshold, so the walk artefact is absent and the run requirements cannot be met either."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes per-team monthly budgets with an 80 percent alert routed to the team lead, which meets the walk artefact, but it describes no pre-call enforcement at a gateway, degradation ladder, or exception logging, so it does not reach run."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The statement describes caps enforced at the gateway before the call, a per-product degradation ladder, and a weekly-reviewed exceptions log, which meets all run artefact requirements, and it does not cancel or contradict the walk artefact of per-team budgets with threshold alerts, so the walk artefact is included by the rubric's inheritance clause."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement is a bare adjective-laden claim ('robust budget controls across the organisation') that does not describe any specific artefact such as per-team budgets with threshold alerts, so it cannot be credited with walk or run."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes caps written into the agent framework configuration that stop agents when hit, which is an enforcement mechanism inside the framework rather than the required per-team budgets with threshold alerts (walk) or gateway-level pre-call enforcement with a degradation ladder and exception logging (run), so neither higher level is supported."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes hard caps at the gateway for two products and an 80 percent alert for the other five, which supports a per-product alert threshold (walk) but not run, since it does not mention a degradation ladder or logged exceptions and the alert-only setup for five products does not evidence caps enforced before the call across the estate; also, per-team budgets are not explicitly described, so walk is the highest level the statement clearly supports."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement 'Everything is pay as you go' describes no commitment artefact at all, so it does not meet the walk requirement of one commitment sized from measured usage, and therefore cannot meet run either."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes one commitment sized from three months of measured usage, which meets the walk artefact, but it does not describe any model-change scenario modelling, exit terms, or shortfall exposure tracking, so the run requirements are not met."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The statement describes an artefact of commitments each modelled against three model-change scenarios, with exit terms summarised and shortfall exposure tracked monthly, which satisfies the run requirements, and since it implies no contrary clause, the walk artefact (one commitment sized from measured usage) is taken to be included."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes negotiating posture ('negotiate hard', 'strong commercial terms') rather than any artefact, such as a commitment sized from measured usage, so it does not meet the walk requirement and therefore cannot reach run."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes one commitment sized from measured usage, which meets the walk artefact, but the plan to model a model-change effect at renewal is an intention rather than an existing artefact, so the run requirements are not met."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes monthly modelling of shortfall exposure for a commitment sized from a vendor's forecast rather than measured usage, which fails the walk requirement of a commitment sized from measured usage, so it falls to crawl."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The company's statement says nobody has written down who may change a model or a cap, which describes the absence of a written policy and recurring review, so the walk artefact is not present and the run level cannot be reached."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a written AI cost policy and a recurring (biweekly) review by named leads, which meets the walk artefacts, but it describes no policy-as-code, reproducible evidence pack, or gate on model changes, so run is not supported."}

{"level": "run", "reason": "The statement describes policy as code, a reproducible evidence pack rebuilt from the ledger with one command, and a gate that blocks model changes lacking cost and quality approval, which together satisfy the run artefacts; it does not mention a written policy or recurring review, but the rubric's inheritance clause lets the run statement include the walk artefact unless the statement says or implies otherwise, and nothing here cancels it."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes only adjectives and a general claim of a 'mature framework' without naming any written policy, recurring review, policy as code, evidence pack, or model-change gate, so no walk or run artefact is described."}

{"level": "walk", "reason": "The statement describes a written policy and a regular review, which satisfies the walk artefacts, but it describes no policy as code, reproducible evidence pack, or model-change gate, and 'mostly enforced by convention' indicates these run artefacts are absent, so the highest supported level is walk."}

{"level": "crawl", "reason": "The statement describes policy as code and a rebuildable evidence pack, but explicitly says model changes ship without a gate, so the run requirement of a gate on model changes is not met, and the statement does not describe a written policy with a recurring review, so the walk requirement is also not evidenced."}
